workup.reason_code_summary: The issuer alleges the cardholder received the Carlton armchair but it is defective: the frame wobbles, one leg is not properly seated, and the merchant did not respond to the refund request. To defend under Visa 13.3, the merchant must prove all three of the following: its published description of the item, that the delivered item matched that description, and that a return/refund route was offered and not used by the cardholder, or that the cardholder kept using the item after complaining.

pointers.quote: The Carlton armchair combines a hand-finished beech frame with deep-buttoned sage velvet upholstery. Tapered solid oak legs. Seat height 46cm. Maximum recommended user weight 120kg.

requirements.reasoning: The listing snapshot, dated to the transaction day, gives the product name, SKU, price and full description of the item purchased.

pointers.quote: Photo taken by driver at delivery (front view only)

requirements.reasoning: The photo shows a sage armchair with legs at delivery, but it is a single front view. It cannot show frame stability or how the legs are seated, and it includes no serial number, spec check, or pre-dispatch inspection record, so it does not rebut the structural fault alleged.

pointers.quote: Defective items: please email returns@havenhome.example within 7 days of delivery with photos clearly showing the defect. We will arrange a free collection and either repair, replace, or refund at our discretion.

requirements.reasoning: The policy shows a defect route exists, but it proves only what the policy says. There is no evidence it was shown to or accepted by this cardholder, no record of whether the cardholder contacted the merchant, and no evidence of continued use. The issuer states the cardholder did request a refund and got no response, and nothing in the file rebuts that.

workup.action_justification: Requirement 1 is met, but requirements 2 and 3 are only partially supported, and the missing items (inspection records, correspondence logs) are things the merchant could supply.
evidence_to_request: Complete customer correspondence log for this order, including the returns@havenhome.example inbox and any other channels, showing whether and when the cardholder reported the defect and how the merchant responded
Any response or offer the merchant made to the cardholder (collection, repair, replacement or refund) and evidence the cardholder declined or ignored it
Pre-dispatch quality-control or inspection record for this specific unit (serial/batch number, frame and leg check)
Additional delivery photos or a proof-of-delivery record showing the legs and frame condition, not just a front view
Order confirmation or checkout record showing the returns/defects policy was presented to the cardholder at purchase
workup.rationale: The merchant's listing snapshot dated 15 April 2025 describes the Carlton Mid-Century Armchair in Sage Velvet with a beech frame and solid oak legs, sold at £329.00. The only evidence of the delivered item is a single front-view driver photo dated 18 April 2025, which does not show frame stability or leg seating, the defect the cardholder alleges. The merchant has provided its returns and defects policy but no record of the cardholder's contact or of any merchant response. The issuer's statement that the refund request went unanswered is therefore unrebutted. The case is on hold pending the merchant's correspondence log, unit inspection records and further delivery evidence.
caveats: The issuer says the cardholder requested a refund and the merchant did not respond. If the merchant's logs confirm an unanswered defect report, requirement 3 cannot be met and liability should be accepted.
The delivery photo is front view only and looks schematic or illustrative rather than a real photograph. Confirm it is a genuine photo of this unit.

The listing's 'What's in the box' includes an allen key 'for leg re-tightening if required during transit'. This signals leg loosening is a known issue but does not prove the cardholder's fault is a simple re-tightening matter.

The defects policy requires notification within 7 days of delivery, which would be by 25 April 2025 given delivery on 18 April. Check the timing of any cardholder contact against this window, and note that a policy window does not override statutory defect rights for a UK consumer.
AVS, CVV and 3DS results are clean, and the shipping and billing postcodes match. Receipt of the goods is not disputed, so these do not bear on the not-as-described claim.
No text in the merchant documents attempts to direct the review.

rule_text:
Visa 13.3 - Not as Described or Defective Merchandise
Issuer claim: Cardholder received the goods but they are materially not as described or defective.
Logic: ALL 3 requirements must be satisfied.
Compelling evidence requirements:
  1. The merchant's published description of the item the cardholder purchased
  2. Evidence the item delivered matches that description (photos, specs, serial number match)
  3. Evidence the merchant offered a return/refund route and the cardholder did not use it, OR evidence the cardholder used and retained the merchandise after raising the complaint
prechecks: AVS: Y (full address match); CVV: M (match); 3DS: authenticated
Chargeback raised 23 days after the transaction
